fields.description: Denormalised from the row. Half of the unique constraint that makes settlement idempotent across batches.
fields.label: Transfer Id

fields.description: The matched record's doctype: Project Payments (read-only reconciliation) or Project Expenses / Non Project Expenses (settlement).
fields.label: Target Doctype

fields.description: The target's own amount at match time. Kept so a fan-out group's sum can be compared against the bank amount without re-reading every target.
fields.label: Target Amount

fields.description: Always Settled. This table records SETTLEMENTS ONLY -- a row here means money was written: a payment or expense marked Paid, or an expense created at Paid. The v2 kind 'Reconciled' (matched, nothing written) was retired at the v3 reversal, because a suggestion and a settlement addressing the same record would contend for the (transfer_id, target_doctype, target_name) unique constraint -- which IS this feature's idempotency guarantee. The field is kept as a Select rather than dropped so the intent stays legible and a future write kind has somewhere to go.
fields.label: Match Kind

fields.description: HOW the counterpart was FOUND -- the tier of the matching ladder, copied from the import row at settlement. 'reference' = the bank reference equals a stored UTR; 'account+IFSC' = the transfer went to a vendor's bank account and the amounts agree within Re 1; 'project in remark' = the amounts agree within Rs 5 and the remark names the record's project; 'Manual' = the matcher found nothing and a person chose the target outright. WARNING: the options were previously 'Bank reference / Vendor+amount+date / Manual', which named NO tier the matcher actually produces -- so 'Manual' was the only valid value and every settlement was stamped with it, including 843 of 849 that the machine had found. The vocabulary is now the matcher's own (services/outflow_import/matcher.py TIER_* constants), the same one Outflow Import Row.match_basis has always used. Whether a PERSON accepted or overrode that suggestion is a DIFFERENT question and lives in settlement_origin.
fields.label: Match Basis
fields.options:
reference
account+IFSC
project in remark
Manual

fields.description: Whether this settlement took the machine's suggestion. 'Suggestion accepted' = the matcher proposed this exact record and a person confirmed it unchanged. 'Suggestion overridden' = the matcher proposed a DIFFERENT record and the person chose this one instead. 'No suggestion' = the matcher offered nothing and the person found the record themselves. DELIBERATELY NOT CALLED 'AUTO': a human clicks confirm on every one of these, so 'accepted' is true where 'automatic' would not be. This is a DIFFERENT question from match_basis, which says which TIER found the counterpart, and from Outflow Import Row.auto_matched, which says only that a suggestion existed at all. Written in the same insert as match_basis so the two cannot drift.
fields.label: Settlement Origin
fields.options:
Suggestion accepted
Suggestion overridden
No suggestion

fields.description: Who confirmed the match (frappe.session.user). Data, not Link, per the house convention for actor fields.
fields.label: Matched By
